title: The relative Cech nerve is one-coskeletal
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category [def-weil-size-convention], and let $f:F\to G$ be a morphism of presheaves of sets, that is, functors $\mathcal C^{op}\to\mathrm{Set}$. Form the simplicial presheaf $E$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] with $E_q=F\times_G\cdots\times_G F$ ($q+1$ factors), faces deleting factors and degeneracies repeating factors; its augmentation to the constant simplicial presheaf $G$ is the common image under $f$. Then $E$ is $1$-coskeletal: its canonical map $E\to\operatorname{cosk}_1\mathrm{sk}_1E$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton] is an isomorphism. More precisely, for every simplicial presheaf $T$, restriction gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(T,E)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(\mathrm{sk}_1T,\mathrm{sk}_1E)$, and both sets identify with $\{g:T_0\to F\mid fgd_0=fgd_1:T_1\to G\}$. In particular, if $a:T\to G$ is an augmentation and $g:T_0\to F$ satisfies $fg=a_0$, it determines a unique simplicial map $T\to E$ with degree-zero map $g$; its degree-$q$ map is the tuple of $g$ applied to the $q+1$ vertices, and this map commutes with the augmentations to $G$.

source.place: Stacks Tag 018I, label lemma-cosk-minus-one, including the displayed morphism bijection and its vertex-tuple construction. Applied to the presheaf category, which has objectwise fibre products.

proof.text: Work with the concrete fibre-product model: for $U\in\mathcal C$, $E_q(U)$ is the set of tuples $(x_0,\ldots,x_q)$ in $F(U)^{q+1}$ with $f_U(x_i)=f_U(x_j)$ for all $i,j$. Restriction along $r:V\to U$ applies $F(r)$ to every coordinate; naturality of $f$ preserves the equalities. For $\alpha:[m]\to[q]$, set $E(\alpha)(x_0,\ldots,x_q)=(x_{\alpha(0)},\ldots,x_{\alpha(m)})$. Selecting coordinates respects identity and composition and commutes with restrictions, so this is the simplicial presheaf in the statement, with faces deleting and degeneracies repeating coordinates. Its augmentation $e_q:E_q\to G$ sends a tuple to the common value $f(x_i)$; coordinate selection preserves this value.

A $1$-truncated map $h:\mathrm{sk}_1T\to\mathrm{sk}_1E$ has $h_0=g:T_0\to F$. Commuting with the two faces forces $h_1=(g d_1,g d_0)$, because on $E_1$ the maps $d_1,d_0$ are respectively the first and second coordinate. Such a tuple lies in $F\times_GF$ exactly when $fgd_0=fgd_1$. Conversely this equality defines that presheaf map $h_1$, and $h_1s_0=(g,g)$ since $d_0s_0=d_1s_0=\mathrm{id}$; hence it also commutes with the degeneracy. These equations check every operator between $[0]$ and $[1]$: besides identities they are the two vertex inclusions, the unique collapse, and the two constant endomorphisms of $[1]$, which are their composites. This gives the asserted bijection between truncated maps and the displayed set of $g$.

source.place: Tag 018I, first diagram of the proof; degeneracy and constant-operator checks expanded

proof.text: Now fix $g:T_0\to F$ with $fgd_0=fgd_1$. For $0\leq i\leq q$ let $v_i^q=T([0]\to[q],0\mapsto i):T_q\to T_0$. If $i<j$, the map $\beta_{ij}:[1]\to[q]$ with endpoints $i,j$ gives $v_i^q=d_1T(\beta_{ij})$ and $v_j^q=d_0T(\beta_{ij})$. Composing the assumed equality with $T(\beta_{ij})$ gives $fgv_i^q=fgv_j^q$. Thus define $H_q:T_q\to E_q$ by $H_q(t)=(gv_0^q(t),\ldots,gv_q^q(t))$; its coordinates have equal image under $f$. For $q=0$ the formula is simply $H_0=g$, with no pairwise condition to check. Each $gv_i^q$ is a presheaf map, so the tuple formula commutes with restrictions along every $V\to U$ and defines a presheaf map $H_q$.

source.place: Tag 018I, construction of g_{n,i} and the edge diagram

proof.text: For any order-preserving $\alpha:[m]\to[q]$ and any $0\leq i\leq m$, functoriality gives $v_i^mT(\alpha)=v_{\alpha(i)}^q$, since $\alpha\circ(0\mapsto i)=(0\mapsto\alpha(i))$. The $i$th coordinate of $H_mT(\alpha)$ is therefore $gv_{\alpha(i)}^q$, which is also the $i$th coordinate of $E(\alpha)H_q$. Equality of all coordinates gives $H_mT(\alpha)=E(\alpha)H_q$. Consequently $H$ is a simplicial map; this verifies both faces and degeneracies, including non-injective $\alpha$, rather than leaving simplicial compatibility implicit.

source.place: Tag 018I, the sentence leaving verification of the simplicial morphism to the reader, written out

proof.text: If $H':T\to E$ is any simplicial map with $H'_0=g$, naturality for the vertex inclusion $[0]\to[q]$ says $\operatorname{pr}_iH'_q=gv_i^q$. Equality of tuples forces $H'_q=H_q$ in every degree. Conversely any simplicial map gives the edge equality by its degree-one component, as in Step 2. Thus $H\mapsto H_0$ is a bijection from full simplicial maps to exactly the same set of $g$ as for truncated maps. The construction in Steps 3--4 restricts in degree one to $(gd_1,gd_0)$, so these two bijections identify the restriction map itself with the identity on that set. This proves precisely the restriction bijection in the statement.

source.place: Tag 018I, uniqueness and both displayed morphism bijections

proof.text: The restriction bijection says directly that $(E,\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{sk}_1E})$ satisfies the defining universal property of a $1$-coskeleton of $\mathrm{sk}_1E$, so the required coskeleton exists. For any chosen representative $(K,\varepsilon)$ of that coskeleton, let $\eta:E\to K$ correspond to $\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{sk}_1E}$, so $\varepsilon\,\mathrm{sk}_1\eta=\mathrm{id}$. By Step 5 with $T=K$, there is a unique $b:K\to E$ restricting to $\varepsilon$. Then $\mathrm{sk}_1(b\eta)=\varepsilon\,\mathrm{sk}_1\eta=\mathrm{id}$, so injectivity in Step 5 gives $b\eta=\mathrm{id}_E$. Also $\varepsilon\,\mathrm{sk}_1(\eta b)=\mathrm{sk}_1b=\varepsilon$, so injectivity in the defining coskeleton bijection with source $K$ gives $\eta b=\mathrm{id}_K$. Hence the canonical map $\eta$ is an isomorphism, without invoking an uncited representability theorem.

source.place: Tag 018I, last assertion, expanded using the universal property of coskeleton (section-coskeleton, equation-cosk)

proof.text: Finally let $a:T\to G$ be the given augmentation, meaning a simplicial map to the constant simplicial presheaf $G$, and suppose $fg=a_0$. Its naturality gives $fgd_0=a_0d_0=a_1=a_0d_1=fgd_1$, so Steps 3--5 supply the unique $H$ with $H_0=g$. For every vertex, $a_0v_i^q=a_q$ by the same naturality. Therefore $e_qH_q=fgv_i^q=a_q$ for every $q$, so $H$ commutes with the augmentations. The formula for $H_q$ is exactly the vertex tuple already constructed, proving every clause of the final assertion.

lean.statement: theorem cechNerve_one_coskeletal {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (f : F ⟶ G) : let P := Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u let E := (Arrow.mk f).cechNerve IsIso ((SimplicialObject.coskAdj (C := P) 1).unit.app E) ∧ ∀ (T : SimplicialObject P), Function.Bijective (fun h : T ⟶ E => (SimplicialObject.truncation 1).map h) ∧ Nonempty ((T ⟶ E) ≃ {g : T.obj (Opposite.op ⦋0⦌) ⟶ F // T.map (SimplexCategory.δ 0).op ≫ g ≫ f = T.map (SimplexCategory.δ 1).op ≫ g ≫ f}) ∧ ∀ (a : T ⟶ (SimplicialObject.const P).obj G) (g : T.obj (Opposite.op ⦋0⦌) ⟶ F), g ≫ f = a.app (Opposite.op ⦋0⦌) → ∃ H : T ⟶ E, (H.app (Opposite.op ⦋0⦌) ≫ Limits.WidePullback.π (fun _ : Fin 1 => f) 0 = g ∧ H ≫ (Arrow.mk f).augmentedCechNerve.hom = a ∧ ∀ (q : ℕ) (i : Fin (q + 1)), H.app (Opposite.op ⦋q⦌) ≫ Limits.WidePullback.π (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => f) i = T.map (SimplexCategory.const ⦋0⦌ ⦋q⦌ i).op ≫ g) ∧ ∀ H' : T ⟶ E, (H'.app (Opposite.op ⦋0⦌) ≫ Limits.WidePullback.π (fun _ : Fin 1 => f) 0 = g ∧ H' ≫ (Arrow.mk f).augmentedCechNerve.hom = a) → H' = H
